title: Treasure Map

serves.summary: The child hears position clues (next to, between, around, through, across) and taps squares on a map to walk a route that follows every clue in order to the treasure, which shows understanding and following position words and prepositions in spoken directions.

request.topic: Following position words to trace a route
request.objective: Listen to position clues (next to, between, around, through, across) and trace a route on a map that follows every clue in order to the treasure. (LA004-05-F, LA004-05-H)

problems.ask: Walk to the treasure. On the way, walk next to the big rock.
problems.goal: The path ends on the treasure and passes a square beside the rock (above it is off the map, so beside or below).

problems.ask: Walk to the treasure. First walk next to the house, then walk between the two trees.
problems.goal: The path touches the house, then steps on the one square between the trees, then ends on the treasure. Passing beside one tree does not count.

problems.ask: Walk to the treasure. Walk next to the big rock, then around the pond, then between the two trees.
problems.goal: The path touches the rock, goes past the pond without stepping in, steps between the trees, and ends on the treasure.

route: next to the pond and the tree
next to the pond and the tree

problems.ask: Walk to the treasure. Go through the tunnel, then across the bridge.
problems.goal: The path enters the tunnel square, then the bridge square, never steps in the river, and ends on the treasure. Going around the hill is not through it.
